task_contract.anchor_definition: The anchor is the first target-specific value-construction function on the dynamic behavior chain: the earliest function, after routing and browser/media signal preparation, whose own body constructs the target observable media fingerprint hash value rather than merely collecting environment signals, dispatching control, packaging the result, or emitting it to the sink.

runtime_boundary.event_plane: DOM CustomEvent on the main document

evidence: The DevTools-visible JavaScript corpus is a single obfuscated bundle and no source map is exposed to the agent.
The target field name and observable action are assembled from character-code arrays at the sink, so direct literal search is insufficient.
The fingerprint hash is carried through runtime-derived transport keys and recovered shortly before console output.
The probe route selects its live configuration only after click-time DOM, control-order, style and dataset state are captured.

The click path crosses delegated event handling, action routing, gate checks, browser and media-capability signal collection, tuple construction, asynchronous scheduling, local event dispatch, runtime slot materialization, fingerprint hashing, dynamic transport and sink wrapping.
The same probe interaction emits non-target shadow/audit objects carrying fingerprint-like values before the target media.fingerprint object.
The deployed bundle also contains proof-like and vendor-like decoys that execute or remain reachable-looking without feeding the target media_fp field.
The target value is separated from the click by Promise, microtask, timer, animation-frame, MutationObserver and DOM CustomEvent boundaries.
The selected runtime configuration is cloned and mutated in a WeakMap-backed materialization step before the fingerprint encoder receives the signal bytes.
The final sink receives an already encoded fingerprint after dynamic cell and lane recovery, so sink inspection alone does not identify the construction site.

behavior_category.reason: The observable value is a stable hash over browser and media-capability environment signals (user agent, platform, language, screen geometry, device pixel ratio, timezone and codec support) combined with the probe configuration. It is not a request signature, stable UI state encoding, byte-array transform or request-body rewrite.

near_categories.why_not: The output has no proof/token/seal request-binding semantics; proof-like code in the bundle is decoy material and does not feed the target field.
The target is dominated by browser/device capability collection, not a compact encoding of UI/form/configuration state.
No network request body is emitted or rewritten; the target is a console-observable fingerprint hash.
